assertions.title: Start converges to one healthy live state with coherent status metadata

steps.expected: Stopped baseline with compatible quality before launch
steps.observed: Baseline status was stopped and quality returned ok=true.

steps.expected: 200/starting followed by convergence to one healthy live state
steps.observed: HTTP 500 with detail ending in stream_e779c08a-d87b-4fa7-be11-bfd5b1be4cdd: available plus a long supervisorctl available list.

steps.action: Manual continuation after recording failure: container-local symlink for the seeded asset path, then supervisorctl add/start for stream_e779c08a-d87b-4fa7-be11-bfd5b1be4cdd
steps.expected: Only used to continue downstream assertions; not needed for VAL-STREAM-008 to pass
steps.observed: Manual start reached RUNNING and status samples showed growing live_duration_seconds/total_duration_seconds and idle restart metadata, but daily_limit_seconds and remaining_daily_seconds stayed null.

evidence.network: GET /status -> 200 stopped; GET /quality -> 200 ok=true; POST /start -> 500 Internal Server Error (available list); manual supervisorctl add/start -> RUNNING; follow-up GET /status -> 200 running.

assertions.issues: The API start never succeeded on the real user surface; it returned the known supervisor available-list 500. Reaching a live state required both a manual supervisorctl add/start and a container-local symlink because the seeded asset storage_path pointed at a host-only absolute path. Even after the workaround, quota counters stayed null.

assertions.title: Stop clears phantom runtime state

steps.action: While the stream was live, kill the underlying runner PID from the supervisor-managed process
steps.expected: Underlying process exits before the API stop request so the stop path clears phantom runtime state
steps.observed: Killed pid 627; supervisor transitioned to STARTING for the same program.
HTTP 500 with body {"detail":"stream_e779c08a-d87b-4fa7-be11-bfd5b1be4cdd: removed process group"}.

steps.expected: is_running=false with no ghost live state

evidence.network: Process kill sequence -> supervisor STARTING; POST /stop -> 500 removed process group; GET /status -> 200 stopped/is_running=false.

assertions.issues: The control plane eventually cleared the ghost running state, but the stop API itself failed with HTTP 500 instead of returning a stopped status payload.

assertions.title: Stale heartbeat converts false-running streams into recoverable errors

steps.action: Inspect backend/streams/.runtime-heartbeats while the stream was live
steps.expected: A heartbeat file exists for the running managed stream and can be expired for the test
steps.observed: No heartbeat file existed for e779c08a-d87b-4fa7-be11-bfd5b1be4cdd; the directory was absent until I created it manually for the simulation.

steps.action: Recreate a live state on the same stream after VAL-STREAM-009
steps.expected: API start or documented manual continuation reaches a live state again
steps.observed: POST /start again returned the same 500 available list; manual supervisorctl add brought the program back to RUNNING.

steps.action: Inject an expired heartbeat file at backend/streams/.runtime-heartbeats/e779c08a-d87b-4fa7-be11-bfd5b1be4cdd.json and query /status immediately
steps.expected: Status leaves healthy live state and exposes recoverable restart/error metadata
steps.observed: HTTP 200 status=error with is_running=false and runtime_restart.state=scheduled plus next_restart_at/last_failure_at.

steps.action: Poll /status again after the scheduled recovery attempted
steps.observed: Status stayed non-live/error, but the error_message changed to an auto-restart dispatch failure caused by the same supervisor available-list 500 while supervisor still reported the program RUNNING.

evidence.network: Initial heartbeat directory check showed no file; POST /start retry -> 500 available list; manual supervisorctl add -> RUNNING; injected stale heartbeat then GET /status -> 200 error with scheduled restart metadata; later GET /status -> 200 error with auto-restart dispatch failure.

assertions.issues: The managed runner never emitted the expected heartbeat file on its own, so the stale-heartbeat scenario could only be exercised by manually creating an expired file. The status surface does move into a recoverable error when that file exists, but the real runtime surface is missing the heartbeat artifact needed for the contract, and the scheduled recovery then hits the same supervisor available-list failure.

assertions.title: Backend restart preserves healthy managed streams with one authoritative post-restart state

steps.action: Capture health, status, supervisor status, and logs while the stream was live
steps.expected: One healthy live state before restart
steps.observed: Health was healthy; API status and supervisorctl both reported one RUNNING stream program.

steps.action: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml restart backend while the runner remained live
steps.expected: Backend recovers and preserves the same live stream record without duplicate state
steps.observed: Health polling returned 000/000/200 across the restart and the same stream id came back as running; supervisor still showed a single RUNNING pid.

steps.action: Run one follow-up control action on the same stream record (POST /stop in the phantom-runtime test)
steps.expected: Control action succeeds cleanly after restart
steps.observed: The control action returned HTTP 500 removed process group instead of a successful stopped response.

evidence.network: GET /health pre-restart -> 200 healthy; GET /status pre-restart -> 200 running; docker compose restart backend -> health 000,000,200; GET /status post-restart -> 200 running; POST /stop follow-up -> 500 removed process group.

assertions.issues: The backend restart preserved a single live runtime, but the required post-restart control action did not work cleanly because POST /stop failed with HTTP 500. The immediate pre/post-restart log snapshots were also empty, which limited operator confirmation during the restart window.

assertions.title: Backend and runtime restart reconcile running-stream state without duplicate ownership

steps.action: Restart the backend while the same rehearsal stream stayed live on the runner
steps.expected: Health returns and the same stream record reconciles without duplicate ownership
steps.observed: Health returned to 200 quickly and both API status and supervisorctl showed one running stream after restart.

steps.action: Compare log and status surfaces around the restart
steps.expected: Status and logs remain consistent again after restart
steps.observed: Status stayed coherent, but the immediate pre/post-restart log endpoint snapshots were empty even though later stream.log inspection showed active FFmpeg output.

steps.action: Use one control action on the same stream record after restart
steps.expected: A stop/refresh/restart action works without duplicate running state
steps.observed: POST /stop returned HTTP 500 removed process group; follow-up status was stopped/is_running=false, so the state cleared but the control action was not healthy.

evidence.network: Restarted backend: /health -> healthy after two empty replies; /status stayed one running record; /logs snapshots were empty during the restart window; POST /stop -> 500, then GET /status -> 200 stopped/is_running=false.

assertions.issues: The restart reconciled back to one running record, but the post-restart operator path was not fully coherent: the log surface was empty during the restart window and the follow-up stop control returned HTTP 500 instead of succeeding cleanly.

frictions.description: The documented API start flow immediately failed with the known supervisor available-list 500, so I had to record that failure and then use docker exec supervisorctl add/start on the assigned stream to continue downstream assertions.
frictions.resolution: Recorded the failing API response in VAL-STREAM-008 evidence, then used manual supervisorctl add/start only to continue later assertions on the same stream.

frictions.description: The seeded copy asset existed at /app/uploads inside the runner, but the DB storage_path pointed at a host-only absolute path (~/Documents/Work/youtube_translation/backend/uploads/...), so the runner crashed with FileNotFoundError until I added a container-local symlink.
frictions.resolution: Created a temporary symlink inside youtube-streaming-runner from the host-style storage_path to /app/uploads/... for the assigned asset, then removed it during cleanup.

frictions.description: The managed stream never created backend/streams/.runtime-heartbeats/e779c08a-d87b-4fa7-be11-bfd5b1be4cdd.json on its own, so the stale-heartbeat flow required manual stale-file injection instead of expiring an emitted heartbeat.
frictions.resolution: Created the expected heartbeat directory and injected one expired heartbeat JSON for the assigned stream, captured the status transition, then removed the file during cleanup.

summary: Tested 5 assertions: 0 passed, 5 failed. The real API start path failed with the known supervisor available-list 500; manual supervisorctl and asset-path workarounds were required to reach a live state. Backend restart preserved one running record, but the follow-up stop control still returned 500, and the actual managed runner did not emit heartbeat files without manual injection. Final cleanup restored the assigned stream to status=stopped with is_running=false.
